claims.claim:
- Search primary documentation and existing implementations before adding a solution. Reuse library APIs where they fit, and record the exact source and adaptation in `docs/sources.md`.
- Keep the CLI/pipeline thin. Put simulator mechanics in runtime, statistics in analysis, artifact I/O in storage, and report rendering in reporting. Prefer a small reusable function over duplicated condition logic.
- Use `uv`, the local `.venv`, `.env`, and the committed lockfile. Never commit credentials, local environments, or authentication caches.
- Add manually written comments explaining local mechanics and their role in the experiment. Link authoritative documentation for nontrivial library usage. Keep comments accurate when code changes.
- Write meaningful tests before changes to numerical, simulator, serialization, or intervention behavior. Run the documented user workflow after integration, inspect complete logs and outputs, and fix defects before interpreting results.
- Use timestamped logging. Do not truncate scientific measurements or future LLM prompts/responses; the current experiment does not invoke an LLM. Exclude credentials from logged inputs.
- Report each control's cosine and the odd/even decomposition of the signed responses. These are sign-dependent and sign-independent components, not automatic labels for useful steering and disruption. A slowdown alone does not establish bidirectional speed control or near-optimality. See [statistical assumptions](docs/methodology.md#statistical-assumptions-and-rank-interpretation).
- Before claiming label specificity, compare other extraction labels and random directions. The smallest attainable comparison rank with k controls is 1/(k+1); interpreting it as a calibrated p-value additionally requires exchangeability under an explicit null. Norm matching alone is insufficient. The Ant turning-derived direction has a stronger absolute odd world-Y response than the lateral-derived direction in the later audit ([saved-data verification](reports/fact-check-2026-10-29/verification.json)).
- A travel angle computed from displacement is not independent mechanism evidence. Shared-baseline even parts require joint seed resampling. Check the baseline–treated covariance before claiming that pairing reduced uncertainty ([methodology](docs/methodology.md)). First-layer activations depend on observations; a fitted constant intervention vector does not. A projection onto the response to a specified observation change and a separate observation intervention can test a perceptual explanation, subject to the clipped-wrench qualification below.
- Before calling seeds fresh, check all reserved cohorts, including application seeds omitted from the original manifests. Treat prior audit conclusions as claims to verify against artifacts. Report Monte Carlo estimates at their floor as estimates, not upper bounds on exact p-values. Keep historical test records distinct from checks actually repeated in the current task.
- Keep development checks separate from scientific results. Synthetic tests and random untrained-policy fixtures establish mechanics, not locomotion steering efficacy.
- Keep heading-trend units independent of the window length, report a one-window trend as unavailable, and wrap path-direction differences at the angle branch cut. Finite-horizon geometry does not establish a bounded long-run heading offset; see the [kinematics follow-up](reports/fact-check-2026-10-29/kinematics-follow-up.md).
- Preserve held-out split integrity and immutable selection. Report unsuccessful experiments. Interpret a new hypothesis using fresh confirmation data after earlier results informed the hypothesis.
- Update the experiment register and individual reports with observed results and reasoning. Keep setup in README, methodology in `docs/methodology.md`, source audits in `docs/sources.md`, and findings in `reports` without copying entire sections between them.
- Push working core changes before experiments and training code before training. Use meaningful functional commits and feature PRs, perform one substantive review, and merge passing changes. Publish resulting steering artifacts and any newly trained policy with provenance; reference upstream weights instead of silently repackaging them.

claims.claim: Can a small change inside a frozen reinforcement-learning policy change how it moves, without retraining it? This project extracts a direction from contrasting hidden activations in unsteered rollouts, adds that direction during inference, and tests locomotion against baselines and controls. It uses **no behavioral cloning** and never updates the evaluated policy's weights.

claims.claim: The method adapts [contrastive activation addition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06681) to continuous control, building on [earlier interventions in RL maze policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08043). The contribution is a reproducible locomotion experiment and its evidence, not the invention of activation steering. The Python pipeline combines PyTorch, Stable-Baselines3, Baukit, Gymnasium and MuJoCo with saved-data reporting and an interactive evidence explorer. [Sources and adaptation boundaries](docs/sources.md).

claims.claim: **What we found:** Ant's ground path can shift toward world +Y, with costs to effort, reward or physical reliability. Its original confirmation failed the full acceptance gate. Some controls passed pilot gates. These results support measured intervention effects, not reliable semantic control or generalization across trained policies. claims.claim: Healthy fitting windows define high/low behavior groups. Their episode-weighted activation-mean difference is scaled to the fitting activations' centered RMS. A [Baukit forward hook](https://github.com/davidbau/baukit/blob/9d51abd51ebf29769aecc38c4cbef459b731a36e/baukit/nethook.py) adds `alpha * direction` after the actor's first ReLU; ordinary policy prediction computes the actions. Fitting data, validation data and held-out evaluation have separate roles.

claims.claim: We investigate whether a constant hidden-activation intervention can alter locomotion in a frozen reinforcement-learning policy without behavioral cloning or weight updates. Earlier HalfCheetah attempts produced posture changes and slowdowns but did not establish a useful replicated controller. The featured Ant experiment extracts an episode-weighted difference of activation means from natural world-Y velocity variation and selects intervention strength on separate validation episodes. The locked strength {{alpha}} changes world-Y ground-plane velocity by {{effect}} m/s, paired percentile-bootstrap 95% interval {{ci}}, on {{n}} confirmation pairs, retaining {{retention}}% of mean forward speed. Its status remains `{{status}}`: both arms have {{baseline_failures}}/{{n}} failures and a shared pre-onset ending triggers a strict rejection rule. A later audit reproduces {{fresh_effect}} m/s {{fresh_ci}} on {{fresh_n}} further resets, while failures increase from {{fresh_baseline_failures}} to {{fresh_failures}}. Its sign-dependent response has comparison rank {{random_p}} against {{random_n}} isotropic directions; this is not a calibrated specificity p-value without an exchangeability assumption. Lateral-label specificity is not supported. Projection ablations and an observation intervention support a heading-related explanation, but clipping prevents general physical-heading equivalence. We publish the positive effect, failed quality gates, complete controls, raw episodes, and a saved-data publication workflow. The evidence is specific to the evaluated checkpoint and simulator; cross-training-seed generalization remains untested. [E5, E9; generated values from the accompanying evidence bundle.]

claims.claim:
The [scientific-rigor audit](../reports/scientific-rigor-audit.md) reuses the production estimators and adds three standard tools.
- **Randomization test.** A paired sign-flip test, which is what [SciPy's `permutation_test`](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.14.1/reference/generated/scipy.stats.permutation_test.html) calls `permutation_type="samples"`. Its Monte Carlo p-value is (b+1)/(m+1), following [Phipson & Smyth](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.05766), so it is never zero.
- **Odd/even decomposition.** An exact algebraic split of the responses at ±α into sign-dependent and sign-independent parts.
- **Monte Carlo rank test and paired sample size** (used by the [world-Y specificity audit](../reports/ant-classic-005-y-shift-audit.md)).
  - The rank test is Barnard's Monte Carlo test as reviewed in [Myllymäki et al., *Global envelope tests*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1307.0239): the observed statistic is ranked among s+1 values, giving p = (1 + #≥)/(s+1) with ties counted as extreme. This is the same form as the Phipson & Smyth rule.
  - Sample size uses the paired normal approximation n = ((z₁₋α/₂ + z_power)·σ_d/δ)², following the [CBU statistics wiki](https://imaging.mrc-cbu.cam.ac.uk/statswiki/FAQ/power/onesamp). It slightly underestimates exact paired-t sample sizes. Quantiles come from Python's [`NormalDist.inv_cdf`](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/statistics.html#statistics.NormalDist.inv_cdf).
  - Heading time courses use [`numpy.unwrap`](https://numpy.org/doc/1.26/reference/generated/numpy.unwrap.html).
- **Weak-null reading of the sign-flip test and shared-seed variance** (used by the [path-mechanism audit](../reports/ant-classic-005-mechanism-audit.md)).
  - Exact sign-flip calibration requires symmetry/exchangeability under the sign changes; a zero-mean null alone is insufficient. Without that symmetry, the mean-based test has an asymptotic weak-null interpretation under the relevant regularity conditions (Romano 1990, *JASA* 85:686–692, as reviewed by [Ritzwoller, Romano & Shaikh](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09521)). This does not establish finite-sample exactness for Ant.
  - `sign_flip_pvalue(..., studentized=True)` divides each relabeled mean by its own standard error, following [Chung & Romano 2013](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5939).
  - Monotonicity and continuity conditions can give sufficient guarantees for common-random-number variance reduction ([Glasserman & Yao 1992](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.38.6.884)); they are not necessary conditions, and they have not been established for this experiment. The audit measures the baseline–treated correlation instead of assuming a gain, without equating weak correlation with independence.
- **Second-order optimality conditions.** At an interior local maximizer of a twice-differentiable unconstrained objective, the gradient is zero and the Hessian is negative semidefinite ([lecture notes](https://ee.iitm.ac.in/uday/notes/opt/uo.html); Nocedal & Wright, *Numerical Optimization*, 2nd ed., ch. 2). Applying this to an activation offset requires a local maximum along that intervention path. A trained return objective does not establish local optimality of deterministic evaluation velocity. This motivates a post hoc hypothesis, not evidence for it.

claims.claim:
- **Observation layout.** [Gymnasium Ant-v5 `_get_obs`](https://github.com/Farama-Foundation/Gymnasium/blob/v1.0.0/gymnasium/envs/mujoco/ant_v5.py) concatenates `qpos[2:]`, `qvel` and `cfrc_ext[1:]` clipped to the contact-force range. That puts the torso quaternion at obs[1:5], free-joint velocities at obs[13:19] and 13 × 6 contact wrenches at obs[27:105].
- **Frames.**
  - MuJoCo's ["c"-quantities](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.1.5/computation/index.html) are expressed "in a global frame centered at the subtree center of mass".
  - [`mjData`](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.1.5/APIreference/APItypes.html) lists `cfrc_ext` in rotation:translation order.
  - The free joint's linear velocity is world-frame and its angular velocity body-frame. `tests/test_perception.py` establishes this with [`mj_objectVelocity`](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.1.5/APIreference/APIfunctions.html#mj-objectvelocity). The pages consulted during the audit did not state it, but the [MuJoCo 3.1.5 overview](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.1.5/overview.html#floating-objects) does: linear free-joint velocities are global-frame and rotational ones local-frame.
  - The physical-state comparison deliberately scales contact wrenches below clipping; it verifies the coordinate frames in that regime. Actual Ant observations have already lost saturated wrench values. The historical comparator computes `clip(R clip(f))`, whereas a physically yaw-rotated state's observation would contain `clip(R f)`. These are generally unequal, as the saturated-wrench regression test demonstrates. Quaternion and world-linear-velocity rotations remain exact. Keep the measured observation-intervention outcomes, but interpret the alignment and ablations as support for a heading-related perceptual account, not exact physical-state equivalence or a sole semantic mediator. See the [implementation and tests](../tests/test_perception.py), which preserve the original transform.
- **Statistics.**
  - SciPy 1.14.1 [`bootstrap`](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.14.1/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) supplies the BCa and percentile intervals.
  - [`permutation_test`](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.14.1/reference/generated/scipy.stats.permutation_test.html) with one sample flips signs.
  - [`wilcoxon`](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.14.1/reference/generated/scipy.stats.wilcoxon.html) gives the signed-rank test.
  - The rank arithmetic follows [Phipson & Smyth 2010](https://doi.org/10.2202/1544-6115.1585); calibration additionally requires a justified null and exchangeability. Norm matching a selected contrast against random directions does not establish that assumption. [Project interpretation](methodology.md#statistical-assumptions-and-rank-interpretation).
  - The adjustment uses [Holm 1979](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4615733); its family-wise guarantee requires valid input p-values.
- **Rendering.** The paper renderer draws Greek letters with ReportLab's standard Symbol font and exponents with `<super>` [paragraph markup](https://docs.reportlab.com/reportlab/userguide/ch6_paragraphs/).

claims.claim: The lateral measurement is **world Y**, calculated from the root position before and after integration divided by the actual timestep: [runtime.py:224](../src/rl_locomotion_steering_vectors/runtime.py#L224). Yaw is computed from the normalized scalar-first quaternion, with wrapped angle differences; inversion uses the sign of the body's Z axis projected onto world Z: [runtime.py:132](../src/rl_locomotion_steering_vectors/runtime.py#L132), [runtime.py:163](../src/rl_locomotion_steering_vectors/runtime.py#L163). Forbidden contact resolves the actual named `floor` and `torso_geom` geometries, IDs 0 and 1 in this XML, and requires nonpositive contact distance. Ordinary leg-ground contact is allowed. claims.claim:
- The intervention is causal for this frozen policy under the paired simulator protocol, but fitting association, sign selection, and behavior naming do not establish internal semantics. Only one pretrained policy was studied in this Ant attempt.
- Episode summaries use available post-onset steps; prefix-only episodes receive zero behavioral/time-fraction summaries but still count as failures. Every planned pair remains in the estimator. Episode means, including inversion/contact fractions, receive equal weight rather than being pooled over timesteps. They are not a fixed 45-second outcome after an early termination. Forward-speed retention is a ratio of these mean speeds, not retained distance traveled. Failure rates, individual episodes, and the shared missing post-onset outcome must accompany the average velocity claim.
- The 2,000-resample episode bootstrap describes the observed paired effect. It is not a simultaneous interval over the adaptive research history or a bound proving the population failure increase is below five percentage points. The safety gate uses observed rate differences, which remain uncertain with 30 pairs.
- The cache identity hashes the runtime and treatment inputs; it does not itself hash every dependency, environment source, or analysis file. The manifest pins versions, analysis artifacts record a separate analysis hash, and this audit verified the important installed upstream sources. Those complementary records matter for reproduction.
- No accepted formal replication or calibrated fresh-episode application can be claimed from this run. A later audit reproduced the world-Y effect on fresh resets, with its own failures and limitations. The software's failed status and preserved failed episodes are part of the result, not artifacts to remove.

claims.claim:
- **Policy and environment:** the pinned `farama-minari/Ant-v5-SAC-medium` checkpoint (revision `de5978d…`), deterministic actions, unmodified `Ant-v5`.
- **Episodes:** steering from step 100 (onset) to step 1,000 or termination. The production rollout code (`runtime.run_episode`, `execution.collect_episodes`) and the condition-identity guards are reused.
- **Seeds:** 540000–540019 (n = 20), disjoint from every recorded split (500000–500015, 501000–501063, 510000–510009, 520000–520029, 530000–530029). The replication split stays unused.
- **Arms:** one shared baseline (α = 0). Every direction runs at α = −0.1 and α = +0.1; the perception arms run at ±δ_eq.
- **Directions:** all at norm 5.1513, the fitting activation RMS shared by the saved vectors, unless marked "raw".
  - `lateral` (primary) and `turning` (other-label contrast vector): the saved arrays.
  - `random000`–`random098`: 99 isotropic Gaussian directions, `SeedSequence(540099)`.
  - `shuffled01`–`shuffled19`: the `lateral_shuffled` output of the production estimator `analysis.fit_vectors(fit, ["lateral"], seed=k)` for k = 1…19. These reuse the saved fitting episodes and the original rules.
  - `heading_parallel` (raw), `heading_orthogonal` (raw), `heading_orthogonal_renorm`, `heading_axis_renorm`: the decomposition of `lateral` along ĝ.
    - g is the mean central difference (±2°) of first-ReLU activations when the observed world is rotated about z, over every tenth post-warmup fitting state. The rotation acts on the quaternion, world linear velocity and world-oriented contact wrenches ([`perception.py`](../src/rl_locomotion_steering_vectors/perception.py)).
    - `heading_parallel` + `heading_orthogonal` = `lateral` exactly.
- **Perception arms (no activation edit):**
  - The observed world is rotated by ∓δ_eq after onset; the physics is unchanged.
  - δ_eq = 0.1·(lateral·ĝ)/‖g‖ = **0.160876 rad (9.217°)**. Under linearization, this is the perceived rotation that moves first-layer activations along ĝ as much as α = 0.1 of `lateral` does.
  - A test checks the rotation against physically rotated MuJoCo states.
- **Treatment hashes:** every array and its float32 SHA-256 are in [`directions.npz`](ant-classic-005-independent-audit/directions.npz) and [`directions.json`](ant-classic-005-independent-audit/directions.json).
- **Size:** 124 directions. That is 1 + 2 × 124 + 2 = 251 arms × 20 seeds = 5,020 episodes.

claims.claim: **Which null the sign-flip test addresses.** Exact sign-flip calibration requires symmetry/exchangeability under the sign changes, not merely a zero mean. A perturbation can change trajectories while having zero average effect; chaotic divergence does not prove or disprove that distributional assumption. For a weak zero-mean null without symmetry, validity is asymptotic under the relevant regularity conditions (Romano 1990, *JASA* 85:686–692; reviewed by [Ritzwoller, Romano & Shaikh 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09521)). Studentizing is a robustness device ([Chung & Romano 2013](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5939)), not a finite-sample guarantee for this dataset.

- **Rotation check.** Writing travel angle as atan2(ΔY, ΔX) showed that the 18.0-vs-17.4 m agreement follows from the definition. claims.claim:
**Three readings need correcting:**
1. **The world-Y response is not specific to the lateral label.**
   - The *turning* vector was fitted on yaw-rate labels and is nearly orthogonal to the lateral vector (cosine +0.114). It moves world Y more than the lateral vector at every |α| ≤ 0.2.
   - At −0.1 it would pass the lateral gate: +0.625 m/s, 94.4% speed retention, failures 1→1.
   - The isotropic-random comparison supports specificity only weakly: rank 1 of 7 at |α| = 0.1, p = 1/7.
2. **The selected validation shift has an uncertain sign-independent component.** The original sign-count argument for a generic drift was invalid because directions share one baseline; the correction below supersedes it.
   - *Later correction* ([mechanism audit](ant-classic-005-mechanism-audit.md) §3): every one of these even parts shares a single baseline, so they are not separate pieces of evidence. Resampled jointly, the generic drift is +0.074 [−0.027, +0.164] m/s at |α| = 0.05 and +0.108 [+0.020, +0.187] at 0.1. The quarter (26%) has an interval of about [8%, 39%].
3. **The measured path change accompanies a bounded heading offset.** On average the direction of travel rotates by +3.84°. The time course does not show a continuing turn, and the aggregate body-relative comparison does not support sidestepping toward +Y. Individual paths still wander, as the seed-510000 movie shows.

claims.claim: ## Terms in plain language
claims.independent_check: Headlines and tables checked against independent raw-array calculations. Preserve failed acceptance. Rank inference, semantic naming and optimality claims narrowed. Historical statements in the paper are attributed to their records.

claims.claim:
| Term | Meaning here |
| --- | --- |
| Policy / actor | The neural network that maps the robot's observations to motor commands |
| Reinforcement learning | Learning actions from interaction and rewards, rather than copying demonstration actions |
| SAC | Soft Actor-Critic, a reinforcement-learning algorithm for continuous actions |
| TQC | Truncated Quantile Critics, a reinforcement-learning variant using a distributional value estimate |
| Hidden activation | An intermediate numerical representation inside the actor |
| Steering vector | A fixed list of numbers added to a hidden activation to change the actor's behavior |
| Contrastive activation addition | Subtracting mean hidden activations of contrasting groups and injecting the resulting direction |
| Strength / alpha | The multiplier controlling how much of a direction is added |
| Frozen policy | The actor's learned weights do not change during this experiment |
| Paired episode | Baseline and intervention runs sharing a reset seed and the same state before steering starts |
| Validation | Data used to choose a candidate and its strength |
| Confirmation / replication | Fresh episode sets checking a choice after it has been locked |
| Confidence interval | A bootstrap estimate of uncertainty in the mean paired behavioral change |
| Median / interquartile range | The middle observed value / the interval covering the middle half of observed values |
| Cosine similarity | How similarly two vectors point; 1 means aligned, 0 means perpendicular, and a negative value means opposing components dominate |
| Fitting speed floor | A minimum forward-window speed used only to choose extraction data, not to discard evaluation failures |
| Episode-averaged contact fraction | Average the available post-onset contact indicator within each episode, then weight episode summaries equally; a low average can hide a long failure in one trial |
| Episode physical-failure rate | The fraction of episodes classified as failed before averaging, retaining individual collapses in the quality assessment |
| Prefix-only episode | An episode with no post-onset steps; its behavioral/time-fraction summaries are assigned zero but it still counts as failed, the pair remains counted, and the original strict rule blocks the full quality gate |
| Forward-speed retention | The ratio of steered to baseline episode-averaged forward speeds; it is not distance retention, completion rate, or evidence of full-horizon persistence |
| Lateral velocity | Speed along the world's ground-plane y axis; it is distinct from torso height and does not establish sideways motion relative to the body's heading |
| Effort proxy | Mean squared normalized actions, which is not a measurement of physical energy |
| Useful gate | A predeclared threshold combining behavioral effect, uncertainty, locomotion preservation, and physical-quality limits (failure, inversion and contact rise at most five percentage points; no prefix-only episode) |
| Causal effect | A behavioral difference caused by the controlled activation intervention in the tested system |
| Odd / even response | Halves of the difference and sum of effects at +alpha and −alpha. These measure sign dependence and sign independence. Either can include useful effects or disruption; neither proves semantic steering or its absence. |
| Shuffled-control alignment | Cosine between a label-shuffled control and its primary. A large value means the control re-tests part of the primary direction instead of being a label-free null. |
| Travel angle | Direction of an episode's net ground displacement after steering starts. Its change measures how much the whole path is rotated, without relying on torso orientation. |
| Rank test | Compares one direction's response with k random directions: rank = (1 + number at least as large) / (k + 1). Interpreting this as a calibrated null-hypothesis p-value requires exchangeability of the primary and comparator statistics under that null; matching norms alone does not establish it. |
| Body-relative travel change | Change of the travel direction measured from the torso: travel-angle change minus torso-heading change. It is zero if the whole gait turns rigidly and equals the path change for pure sidestepping. |
| Matched horizon | Compare arms over their common observed steps. This removes unequal averaging durations within a pair, but treatment-related termination still determines that duration; it does not recover an unobserved full-horizon outcome. |
| Arm correlation | Correlation across resets between baseline and treated outcomes. For equal sample sizes, positive covariance reduces the variance of the paired mean difference relative to independent arms with the same marginal variances. A noisy sample correlation does not guarantee narrower realized bootstrap intervals. |
| Perceived-heading direction | Operational name for the first-layer activation response to the specified yaw-like observation transform. Alignment and component interventions support heading involvement, without establishing a unique semantic mediator or exact physical-heading equivalence. See the [current audit](ant-classic-005-independent-audit.md). |
| Perception intervention | Changing the observation supplied to the policy while leaving simulator state unchanged. Here the transform rotates orientation, world linear velocity and already-clipped contact wrenches; it tests the behavioral effect of that specified input change. Clipping limits its interpretation as a physically rotated state. |

claims.independent_check: Analytic boundary cases verify slope units, single-window unavailability, angle wrapping and timestep/span validation. claims.claim:
- The heading slope was degrees per chosen window but labeled degrees per 100 steps. It now multiplies the fitted slope by `100 / window`. A single window returns an unavailable slope (`None`), rather than a fabricated zero. The [NumPy linear-fit definition](https://numpy.org/doc/1.26/reference/generated/numpy.polyfit.html) establishes the independent-variable units.
- Subtracting principal path angles could report an almost full revolution across the ±180° branch cut. Differences now wrap to the shortest signed angle in `[-180, 180)`, consistent with [NumPy's arctan2 range](https://numpy.org/doc/1.26/reference/generated/numpy.arctan2.html). This path-direction statistic does not measure accumulated turns.
- Matching step indices requires equal positive finite simulator timesteps. The helper now checks both arms instead of silently using the baseline timestep for both displacements. Invalid window/prefix lengths fail explicitly.
- A finite-horizon heading offset or small fitted trend does not establish bounded long-run behavior or cessation of turning. Current audit prose and contributor guidance now state this limit. Contact-fraction comments no longer claim statistical unbiasedness from merely counting noncontact steps.
- The original speed and height gates threshold episode means; they do not test temporal persistence. Methodology and paper prose now say so, with a transient-effect example in the [analysis tests](../../tests/test_analysis.py). No historical threshold or outcome was changed.
- A lower confirmation estimate does not diagnose a winner's-curse mechanism or prove unbiasedness. The historical rigor report now separates that observation from the assumptions in [Cawley and Talbot (2010)](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf). It also distinguishes covariance participation ratio from matrix rank and measured alignment from a necessary consequence of shared span. Aligned interventions can still have their effects compared.
- Paper-build instructions now identify generated templates and distinguish current report renderings from preserved run-directory originals. Test documentation separates historical full-suite records from the screened no-model checks performed here.

| Uncertainty | Ten paired reset episodes per condition; 2,000 paired-episode percentile bootstrap resamples, seed 710. Timesteps are not treated as independent replicates. |
| Compute | Native Windows, Python 3.12, CPU Torch, four rollout workers and one Torch thread per worker. Exact package versions and seed lists are in the manifest. |

claims.claim: Delta is treated minus baseline in the behavior's units. Speed/lateral use m/s, height uses m, turning uses rad/s, and effort is mean squared normalized action, not physical energy. Confidence intervals resample paired episodes. Validation selects strengths; confirmation and replication provide fresh evidence when recorded. claims.claim: ## Abstract
claims.independent_check: Headlines and tables checked against independent raw-array calculations. Preserve failed acceptance. Rank inference, semantic naming and optimality claims narrowed. Historical statements in the paper are attributed to their records.

claims.claim: We investigate whether a constant hidden-activation intervention can alter locomotion in a frozen reinforcement-learning policy without behavioral cloning or weight updates. Earlier HalfCheetah attempts produced posture changes and slowdowns but did not establish a useful replicated controller. The featured Ant experiment extracts an episode-weighted difference of activation means from natural world-Y velocity variation and selects intervention strength on separate validation episodes. The locked strength -0.1 changes world-Y ground-plane velocity by +0.402 m/s, paired percentile-bootstrap 95% interval [0.308, 0.491], on 30 confirmation pairs, retaining 96.83% of mean forward speed. Its status remains `confirmation_failed`: both arms have 4/30 failures and a shared pre-onset ending triggers a strict rejection rule. A later audit reproduces +0.462 m/s [0.343, 0.587] on 20 further resets, while failures increase from 0 to 2. Its sign-dependent response has comparison rank 0.05 against 99 isotropic directions; this is not a calibrated specificity p-value without an exchangeability assumption. Lateral-label specificity is not supported. Projection ablations and an observation intervention support a heading-related explanation, but clipping prevents general physical-heading equivalence. We publish the positive effect, failed quality gates, complete controls, raw episodes, and a saved-data publication workflow. The evidence is specific to the evaluated checkpoint and simulator; cross-training-seed generalization remains untested. [E5, E9; generated values from the accompanying evidence bundle.]

claims.claim: Projection ablations and a specified observation transformation support a heading-related account. The observation comparator at negative 9.22 degrees produces +0.903 m/s [0.816, 0.998] without an activation addition. It rotates quaternion and world linear-velocity coordinates, plus world-oriented contact wrenches that Ant already clipped. For those channels the operation is `clip(R clip(f))`, generally different from physical rotation's `clip(R f)`. The physical-frame test covers an unsaturated regime, and the new saturation counterexample documents that boundary. Exact physical-heading equivalence and unique semantic mediation are unestablished.

claims.claim: ## 8. Discussion, limitations and conclusion
claims.independent_check: Headlines and tables checked against independent raw-array calculations. Preserve failed acceptance. Rank inference, semantic naming and optimality claims narrowed. Historical statements in the paper are attributed to their records.

claims.claim: Three distinctions remain essential: extraction association differs from intervention effect; intervention effect differs from practical usefulness; and a control's positive response limits specificity rather than disappearing from the record. The Ant effect is a world-frame path change under a fixed checkpoint. Its failed gate remains a negative result, alongside the earlier HalfCheetah failures.
claims.independent_check: Headlines and tables checked against independent raw-array calculations. Preserve failed acceptance. Rank inference, semantic naming and optimality claims narrowed. Historical statements in the paper are attributed to their records.

claims.claim: The historical audits examine alternative estimands, shared-baseline uncertainty, pairing correlations, sign-dependent versus sign-independent responses, and heading/path kinematics. Their complete numerical evidence remains linked in [E6–E9]. The evaluated alternative estimands retain a positive Ant effect; this is not a guarantee across all possible estimands. A travel angle calculated from displacement supplies no independent mechanism evidence. No finding here establishes a body-relative sideways concept, rigid gait preservation, or superiority across independently trained policies.
claims.independent_check: Headlines and tables checked against independent raw-array calculations. Preserve failed acceptance. Rank inference, semantic naming and optimality claims narrowed. Historical statements in the paper are attributed to their records.

claims.claim: The result is confined to the tested checkpoint, simulator, layer, horizons, resets and strengths. The fresh audit checks a single magnitude. Cross-training-seed robustness, domain shift, real robots, sustained target-following, formal replication and practical application remain untested. The original locally dated protocol cannot be retroactively made preregistered before diagnostics. Upstream training curves and complete training history were not reproduced, and action effort is not physical energy.
claims.independent_check: Headlines and tables checked against independent raw-array calculations. Preserve failed acceptance. Rank inference, semantic naming and optimality claims narrowed. Historical statements in the paper are attributed to their records.

claims.claim: **Conclusion.** The original held-out effect is +0.402 m/s with 96.83% mean forward-speed retention and `confirmation_failed`. The later audit reproduces a target effect but increases observed failures. Its interventions support heading involvement while leaving exact physical-state equivalence and unique mediation unresolved. This is a documented causal effect with explicit limits, not a validated general locomotion controller.

Why this happens:
- Isotropic 256-dimensional directions have cosine SD 1/√256 = 0.0625.
- Shuffled contrasts lie in the span of centered window means, as does the primary. The saved covariance participation ratios, (Σλ)²/Σλ², are 7.45 for Ant and 3.30 for HalfCheetah. These describe variance concentration, not matrix rank or guaranteed confinement to leading principal components. Small nonzero eigenvalues can coexist with a small participation ratio; [numerical rank](https://numpy.org/doc/1.26/reference/generated/numpy.linalg.matrix_rank.html) is a different quantity.
- The reported reshuffle experiment measures substantial overlap for these families. Sharing a span alone does not guarantee large overlap with the primary.

claims.claim:
The pattern above has a compact explanation. It was **formulated after seeing these data** and requires a fresh test.
- Assume, additionally, that the evaluated deterministic policy is a local maximizer of a twice-differentiable return function **along this activation-intervention path**. Then the first derivative vanishes and the second is non-positive, giving R(α) ≈ R(0) + ½R″(0)α² ([second-order necessary conditions](https://ee.iitm.ac.in/uday/notes/opt/uo.html); Nocedal & Wright, *Numerical Optimization*, 2nd ed., ch. 2). Training with SAC/TQC does not establish these assumptions for deterministic evaluation or for hidden-state perturbations.
- Forward velocity is one component of the environment reward, alongside control costs and, for Ant, health/contact terms ([HalfCheetah](https://gymnasium.farama.org/environments/mujoco/half_cheetah/), [Ant](https://gymnasium.farama.org/environments/mujoco/ant/)). A local maximum of total return does not imply a local maximum of velocity alone.
- A descriptor absent as an explicit reward term can still affect return through dynamics, survival and action costs. Under an additional rigid planar-rotation approximation with fixed speed, the forward component contains cos θ; the experiments do not establish that all effects of heading enter only through this term.

groups.check: Analytic boundary cases verify slope units, single-window unavailability, angle wrapping and timestep/span validation. Current helper means and denominators are compared with every published original-confirmation and K1 cohort. This compatibility check is separate from independent historical reference calculations and does not revalidate model behavior or long-horizon dynamics.

All original validation/confirmation paired means, percentile intervals, failures and gates; all original extraction and control arrays; fitting contributors and split halves. Diagnostic narratives beyond these reductions and historical replays are attributed records, not revalidated runtime behavior.

Headlines and tables checked against independent raw-array calculations. Preserve failed acceptance. Rank inference, semantic naming and optimality claims narrowed. Historical statements in the paper are attributed to their records.

Every signed arm; P1/P2/S1/S2/M1/M2 numerical arithmetic; K1 geometry and intervals; original robustness alternatives. E1 fitted-regression claims remain historical and are not re-fitted. Saved neural response axes are inputs, not newly measured derivatives.

Earlier audit conclusions are not authority. Their original episode observations feed the new calculations. Historical test counts, replay equality, source inspections, studentized tests and power calculations are attributed records unless explicitly listed in the new verification. Odd/even semantics, unique degradation and rank-calibration assertions are superseded.

Read Git first records, manifest decisions, logged collection and actual seed sets. Dates are recorded timestamps, not independent proof of push time. Original Ant protocol follows diagnostic start. Reused HC fitting and consumed Ant application reservation remain explicit; preregistrations are unchanged.

Independent reductions and algebra; episode weighting, failure thresholds, matched horizons, sign symmetry, random-ensemble exchangeability. Geometry pairs pre-transition input orientation with the ensuing transition velocity. These estimates do not prove a sole mechanism or unconditional superiority.

Saved-data build/check and static publication workflow exercised. Model-running examples inspected only, not executed. Prior commands/test totals are dated records, not claims of tests performed in this audit.

Read primary CAA, maze and PGS papers; pinned Gymnasium, SB3/TQC, Baukit and PGS implementations; version-matched SciPy and MuJoCo docs. PGS continuous Gaussian score/return/baseline adapter is project-specific and paused. Runtime likelihood/gradient tests were not repeated.

Existing media metadata and saved correspondence artifacts inspected. No simulator replay or policy execution. Hashes bind movie bytes and receipts, but cannot independently prove every pixel corresponds to a recorded state. Camera annotations are not new measurements.

Generated values retain cohort/denominator/estimand labels. Site tests and browser controls operate on saved data. Secondary historical derived fields retain the same qualification as their source report.

Read implementation and historical runtime source fingerprints. No model/simulator execution. Code and comments specify intended mechanics; claims about observed execution need saved evidence. Exact checkpoint parameter identity, neural gradients, action-bias derivation and runtime cleanup remain historical evidence rather than revalidation.

interpretation: A disposition is not blanket verification of every sentence. Numerical checks are named explicitly; historical runtime assertions and uncovered claims remain qualified or unresolved.

primary_sources.claim: CAA uses contrasting language-model activations; episode bins, physical filters and RMS scaling here are adaptations.
Frozen RL activation interventions precede this locomotion project; the maze setting and target differ.
PGS uses reward-weighted activation score gradients; the paused continuous-action adapter is not a completed locomotion experiment.
The released pgs_direction sums trajectory-return-weighted sampled-action score gradients and normalizes.
The pinned PGS source contains an MIT notice, retained in docs/pgs-adaptation.md.
Ant observation layout, force clipping, reward and termination; project root-qpos velocity need not be bitwise identical to the body's xpos velocity used by reward.
HalfCheetah root displacement reward, raw observations and no intrinsic fall termination.
Free-joint translational velocity is global-frame and rotational velocity is local-frame.
SAC actor hidden processing and squashed Gaussian distribution; deterministic evaluation is distinct from training.
TQC actor distribution parameter path and clamping.
Trace edits a selected output and removes its registered hook on context exit; this is a source contract, not a new runtime test.
The installed version supports percentile and BCa bootstrap with paired sample semantics.
Paired one-sample permutation_type=samples implements sign changes; calibration needs the appropriate null symmetry.
Monte Carlo rank-test calibration requires exchangeability; matching norms is not that assumption.
